data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise linking contrasting ideas with but, although, even though, however, despite and in spite of.
learningPoints: Use but to connect simple contrasting clauses.
Use although and even though before clauses.
Use despite and in spite of before nouns or verb-ing forms.
Use however to connect contrasting sentences or ideas.
Avoid combining although with but in the same structure.
Choose the linker that matches the grammatical pattern that follows.

sections.explain: ALTHOUGH is followed by a clause with subject + verb.

words.word: Although it was raining, we went for a walk.
Although the rain, we went for a walk.
Although it was raining, but we went for a walk.

sections.explain: DESPITE is followed by a noun, pronoun or verb-ing form, not a full finite clause without 'the fact that'.

words.word: Despite the rain, we went for a walk.
Despite it was raining, we went for a walk.
Despite of the rain, we went for a walk.

sections.explain: IN SPITE OF is followed by a noun, pronoun or verb-ing form.

words.word: In spite of being tired, she finished the work.
In spite being tired, she finished the work.
In spite of she was tired, she finished the work.

sections.explain: HOWEVER can introduce a contrasting sentence and is normally separated by punctuation.

words.word: The hotel was expensive. However, it was excellent.
The hotel was expensive however it was excellent without punctuation.
The hotel was expensive however but it was excellent.

sections.explain: EVEN THOUGH introduces a clause and often emphasises an unexpected contrast.

words.word: Even though he was ill, he went to work.
Even though his illness, he went to work.
Even though he was ill, but he went to work.
The room was small, but it was comfortable.
The room was small, although but it was comfortable.
The room was small, despite it was comfortable.

sections.explain: DESPITE can be followed by a verb-ing form.

words.word: Despite feeling nervous, she gave a good presentation.
Despite she felt nervous, she gave a good presentation.
Despite of feeling nervous, she gave a good presentation.

sections.explain: Do not normally use ALTHOUGH and BUT together to link the same two clauses.

words.word: Although the journey was long, it wasn't boring.
Although the journey was long, but it wasn't boring.
Despite the journey was long, it wasn't boring.

sections.explain: HOWEVER contrasts with the previous idea and can begin a new sentence.

words.word: I liked the design. However, it was too expensive.
I liked the design. Although, it was too expensive.
I liked the design. Despite, it was too expensive.

sections.explain: Use ALTHOUGH before a clause and DESPITE before a noun phrase.

words.word: Although the weather was bad, the match continued.
Despite the weather was bad, the match continued.
Although the bad weather, the match continued.
